United’s new Rule 6.J.6: AI agents may show fares but cannot buy tickets, even if a human approves
Pulse
United bans AI agents from buying its tickets, seats and upgrades
Rule 6.J.6 applies even when a traveller supervises or approves each step, and reaches  travel agency tools. Can an AI still show United fares to a customer?
by Luis Rijo
November 11, 2026
•
13 min read
Subscribe to Newsletter
Subscribe
Comments
Share
United Airlines today revised its Contract of Carriage to put AI agents on the list of prohibited ticketing practices, next to hidden-city and throwaway ticketing. The new Rule 6.J.6 bars "the use of AI Agents to make, modify or service a Ticket, and/or to purchase any service or product." A companion change to Rule 5.H adds "reservations made, modified or serviced by AI Agents" to the bookings the airline says it will cancel without notice, and a new definition in Rule 1 states that the rule holds "whether or not Passenger or another individual supervises or approves" what the software does.

The contract, headed "revised November 11, 2026," governs the carriage of every passenger and bag on United Airlines, Inc. and on carriers flying as United Express. By its own preamble, a passenger agrees to be bound by it simply "by purchasing a ticket or accepting transportation." The change was reported today by View from the Wing, the travel blog written by Gary Leff, and by InsideFlyer, which credited View from the Wing as the original source.
Add PPC Land to Preferred Sources
In Short
United now forbids using an AI assistant to book, change or manage its tickets, or to buy seats, upgrades or other extras, and it says it can cancel any reservation an AI agent made, even if you watched and approved every step. The rule reaches assistants inside search engines, messaging apps and browsers, and AI tools offered through travel agencies, which covers the kind of booking features Google, OpenAI and Meta have been building. An AI can still look up and show United flights and prices, according to two travel blogs that reported the change, but the purchase itself has to be completed by the customer.
One sentence among the prohibited practices
Rule 6.J of the contract, headed "Prohibited Practices," is where United lists the ways passengers try to get around its fare system. Items one to four cover hidden-city or "Point Beyond" ticketing, throwaway ticketing, back-to-back ticketing and the circumvention of stayover and fare category rules. Item five deals with obtaining "a ticket, service, product, or refund through fraudulent or deceptive means," including payment fraud and chargebacks for services already rendered. Item seven is a catch-all for "any practice that United believes, in its sole discretion, is exploitative, abusive or that manipulates/bypasses/overrides United's fare and ticket rules."
Discover more
Learn AI Tools
Book Flights
Rent Cars
AI agents now occupy item six. According to View from the Wing, the November 11 revision is what added them to the list. The clause is a single sentence, and its verbs do most of the work. "Make, modify or service" reaches past the original booking to changes made afterwards and to the servicing of a Ticket, a term the contract does not define. "Purchase any service or product" extends the prohibition beyond the fare. The new definition lists "flights, seats, upgrades, ancillary products and partner products" among the things an agent might act on, so a paid seat assignment or an upgrade bought by an assistant falls inside the same sentence as the ticket itself.
Placement has consequences. Rule 6.K, the remedies clause that follows the list, applies "where a Ticket is booked, held, purchased and/or used in violation of the law, these rules or any fare rule." Its parenthetical examples name only the four older practices - hidden-city, point-beyond, throwaway and back-to-back ticketing - and not AI agents. Its general wording, though, covers any breach of "these rules," and the eight remedies it lists are not minor. They include invalidating tickets, cancelling the rest of an itinerary, confiscating unused flight coupons, permanently banning a passenger or refusing to board them, charging "the full value of a Ticket" measured against the lowest applicable fare "including after the transportation or service have been provided," deleting miles, revoking Elite status, terminating membership of MileagePlus, United's loyalty programme, and taking legal action. The early coverage of the AI rule concentrated on cancellation.
How United defines an AI agent
The definition, new in Rule 1, is longer than the rule it supports. It reads in full:
"AI Agent means any software or service, including but not limited to an AI assistant, AI agent or AI-enabled browser that takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action, whether or not Passenger or another individual supervises or approves its actions, to discover, search for, book, purchase, ticket, service or manage any product or service offered by or through United, including flights, seats, upgrades, ancillary products and partner products, on behalf of or at the instruction of Passenger or other individual."

Boost SEO Traffic
Four features stand out. The first is "semi-autonomous." Much of what is marketed as agentic AI in consumer products proposes an action and waits for a tap before completing it. Including semi-autonomous software brings those tools inside the definition.
The second is the supervision clause. The usual answer to concerns about software spending money is to keep a human in the loop, with the customer confirming the purchase before it goes through. United's text removes that answer. A customer who watches every screen and approves the final payment is still using an AI Agent, as the contract defines it. View from the Wing put it plainly: human supervision or approval does not get around the rule.
The third is the list of verbs. The definition covers software that acts "to discover, search for, book, purchase, ticket, service or manage." Rule 6.J.6, however, prohibits only making, modifying or servicing a Ticket and purchasing a product. Discovering and searching appear in the definition but not in the prohibition. That gap is the textual basis for what remains allowed, discussed below.
The fourth is the phrase "on behalf of or at the instruction of Passenger or other individual." The rule is not limited to travellers booking for themselves. An assistant used by someone booking for a colleague or relative is covered in the same way.
Three named categories
The definition closes with three examples, introduced as "including but not limited to": "(i) AI assistants built into social media, messaging, search or other consumer platforms; (ii) AI-enabled browsers and standalone AI agents; and (iii) any third-party AI assistant that accesses United through a tool, application or connection provided by a  travel agency or other intermediary."
The contract names no product. Each category, however, matches a type of product PPC Land has covered this year. Meta's Muse, an assistant inside a consumer platform, was the agent Amazon said it had cut off from buying on Amazon.com on September 20, 2026. In search, Google's AI Mode began completing hotel bookings with 10 US partners in August 2026. Among browsers, Google added auto browse to Chrome in July, a feature that lets AI agents book travel and fill forms for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US. Products of this kind are often described as computer use agents, because they operate a website through its visible interface rather than through an integration.
The third category matters most for distribution. Elsewhere, the contract uses the word "agent" in an older sense: Rule 4.A says a reservation is valid when space is confirmed "by UA or an authorized agent of UA," a reference to appointed sellers such as travel agencies. Item (iii) makes clear that an authorised seller does not shelter an AI assistant that reaches United through that seller's tools. An online travel agency can sell United tickets. An AI assistant connected through the agency's app cannot buy them, under the contract's terms.
Cancellation without notice
Rule 5.H, which covers improper reservations, begins: "In addition to exercising any of its remedies in Rule 6 K) below, UA reserves the right to cancel bookings and/or reservations which it deems fraudulent, abusive, illogical, fictitious, which are booked and/or reserved with no intention of flying, or for which the passenger makes a misrepresentation without notice to the passenger or the individual making the booking."
